anchor.quote: Fix a digit width $b$, the number of bits in each radix digit.
Let $m = \lceil n/b \rceil$ be the number of digits in each input.
The digit $u_i$, for $0 \le i \le m-1$, is the $i$-th radix digit of the first input
$v_i$ is the $i$-th radix digit of the second input
The polynomial $U(t)$ has the digits of the first input as coefficients.
The polynomial $V(t)$ has the digits of the second input as coefficients
where the product polynomial is $W(t) = U(t)V(t)$
Its $k$-th coefficient $w_k$ is the sum of $u_i v_j$ over $i+j=k$
